newsitem.title: UK: Police hunt armed woman in London court drama.
newsitem.headline: Police hunt armed woman in London court drama.

text.p: A woman who pointed a pistol at one of Britain's most senior judges judge during an appeal hearing in London was being hunted by armed police on Thursday.

The woman stood up in the public gallery and shouted "I have waited long enough. If anyone moves you will all get shot" before pointing the weapon, held two-handed in front of her, at Lord Justice Roy Beldam, witnesses said.
One judge rushed out to raise the alarm while Beldam, 71, and a woman judge sitting with him appealed to the woman, who spoke with an American accent, to put the weapon down.
Eventually the woman, described as slim and in her early 20s, rushed past the judge's bench and fled down a maze of corridors behind the Royal Courts of Justice.
The central London court complex was sealed off and police stopped anyone trying to leave or enter the building.
"She appeared from the public gallery with what appeared to be a handgun," police said.
Barrister Tom MacKinnon, who was in court, said the woman apparently wanted her appeal to be heard which seemed to involve custody of children.
"The judges all deserve medals, they were so cool and calm," said MacKinnon. "Mrs Justice Bracewell was very calm and told her why don't you put your gun down - let's consider this."

"She told everyone not to move. When the court registrar moved towards her and said he would like to take down details of her case she pointed the gun at him and said no one will get hurt if you don't move, but if anyone moves you will all get shot," MacKinnon said.
